messages.text: Chelsea to host Shakhtar's Champions League home games amid ongoing exile

metadata.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk will play their Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge this season after coming to an agreement with Chelsea to host their European matches while they remain in exile from their Donbas Arena home.
metadata.content: Why are Shakhtar playing at Chelsea? Stamford Bridge to host exiled Ukrainian side's Champions League home games | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Why are Shakhtar playing at Chelsea? Stamford Bridge to host exiled Ukrainian side's Champions League home games Shakhtar Donetsk to play Champions League home campaign at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge for 2026/27 season; Ukrainian champions will play at least four matches in west London where large Ukrainian population is located; Blues able to accommodate Shakhtar after missing out on Europe themselves Friday 21 August 2026 16:43, UK Image: Ukrainian champions Shakhtar will play their European home games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge this season Shakhtar Donetsk will play their Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge this season after coming to an agreement with Chelsea to host their European matches while they remain in exile from their Donbas Arena home. The Ukrainian side had been looking for a new temporary base for their continental games and had been linked with holding them at Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium, but will instead travel several miles towards central London to Chelsea's 40,044-capacity home. At the time of the last UK census in 2021, an estimated 19,000 Ukrainians lived in London while around 45,000 have since arrived in the capital since the Russian invasion of Ukraine began in 2022 with a high proportion settled in west London where Stamford Bridge is located. messages.text: Russell claims Dutch GP Sprint pole with Antonelli, Hamilton on back foot

metadata.summary: George Russell made the ideal start to his attempt to mount a championship fightback in the second half of the 2026 F1 season by claiming pole position for Saturday's Dutch Grand Prix Sprint as nearest title rivals Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top four.
metadata.content: Dutch GP Sprint Qualifying: George Russell claims pole position with title rivals Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton on back foot | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Dutch GP Sprint Qualifying: George Russell claims pole position with title rivals Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton on back foot Watch the Sprint on Saturday at 11am (build-up from 10am) with Qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 21 August 2026 16:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pipped Lando Norris for Sprint pole at the Dutch Grand Prix George Russell made the ideal start to his attempt to mount a championship fightback in the second half of the 2026 F1 season by claiming pole position for Saturday's Dutch Grand Prix Sprint as nearest title rivals Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top four. On F1's first day back on track after the sport's four-week summer break, Russell claimed his third Sprint pole in five attempts this season as his final SQ3 lap of 1:11.567 beat McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to the head of the grid by under a tenth of a second. But championship leader Antonelli was only fifth quickest in the other Mercedes, the Italian teenager's session seemingly compromised after he ran through the gravel on his first lap of SQ1. messages.text: Paredes given TEN-game ban; Argentina fined for Falklands banner

metadata.summary: FIFA have issued Leandro Paredes a 10-game ban for fighting after the World Cup final and handed Argentina an £235,647 fine for displaying a Falklands banner after beating England in the semi-finals.
metadata.content: Leandro Paredes given huge 10-game ban after World Cup final fighting as Argentina punished for Falklands banner | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Leandro Paredes given huge 10-game ban after World Cup final fighting as Argentina punished for Falklands banner Leandro Paredes scrapped with Spain's Gavi after Argentina lost the World Cup final; Paredes handed 10-game ban and there are also suspensions for his team-mates Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada, and Gavi; Argentina fined after players held up Falklands banner after beating England Friday 21 August 2026 15:59, UK Image: Leandro Parades was sent off after the game after starting a brawl with some of Spain's players FIFA have issued Leandro Paredes a 10-game ban for fighting after the World Cup final and handed Argentina an £235,647 fine for displaying a Falklands banner after beating England in the semi-finals. Paredes was involved in ugly scenes after Argentina's extra-time loss to Spain in New York/New Jersey, grabbing opponent Eric Garcia by the throat and then pushing Spain's unused sub Gavi to the ground. Paredes was shown a red card for violent conduct at the time. Paredes' team-mate Nahuel Molina was also involved in the scuffles and tried to knock over Rodri as the Spain captain ran past him. Molina has been handed a seven-game ban. Lewis copped a two-game ban after a Grade C charge for 'dangerous contact' with Warrington Wolves' Ewan Irwin during their rearranged round two fixture on Tuesday. messages.text: 'I'm here to win' - Arsenal announce £55m Konsa deal

metadata.summary: Arsenal have completed the £55m deal to sign defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.
metadata.content: Ezri Konsa: Arsenal complete £55m deal for Aston Villa and England defender | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Ezri Konsa: Arsenal complete £55m deal for Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa completes £55m move to Arsenal from Aston Villa; England defender provides additional competition in defence for the Premier League champions; Konsa's signing comes with William Saliba out for an extended period, plus Jurrien Timber is also injured Friday 21 August 2026 16:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at the best of Ezri Konsa from last season Arsenal have completed the £55m deal to sign defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. "It's a proud moment for me and my family to play for one of the best teams in the world," Konsa said after Arsenal announced the move. "I want to keep winning, hungry to win and that's what I'm here for. I'm here to win. I'll do everything in my power to continue bringing success to this club." The England international has signed a four-year contract with the option of an additional 12 months after passing his medical. He joins for a fixed fee of £51m with a potential £4m in add-ons. The 28-year-old could now make his Arsenal debut against his old club at Villa Park in the Monday Night Football on August 31, live on Sky Sports .
